inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 continuing 'Revenue from contracts with customers' (Premier Retail: Peter Alexander A$565.3m + Smiggle A$230.2m). Excludes A$36.5m Myer transitional-services (TSA) fee income, A$14.3m interest revenue and the Breville associate profit; each of those is handled outside the operating flows (see notes). Pre-FY2025 whole-company revenue (~A$1.6bn) includes the Apparel Brands sold to Myer in Jan-2025 and is NOT the compounding base.
inputs.share_count_basis: 159.522m ordinary shares on issue at 25 July 2026 (FY26 AR share-capital note, after 373,837 shares bought back) plus ~0.74m dilutive performance rights (diluted WANOS 160.518m vs basic ~159.78m). Held FLAT: SBC (A$1.9m) is expensed in the flows; the A$100m on-market buyback (announced Dec-2025, A$4.6m spent to year-end) is value-neutral in this model and only A$4.6m of it has been cash to date.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank loans A$69.0m (secured, now current) less cash A$391.35m at 25 July 2026. Lease liabilities (A$62.4m current + A$89.5m non-current = A$151.8m) are EXCLUDED because the lease cash cost is charged inside the flows (treatment B). The A$71.8m interim dividend paid 20-Aug-2026 out of this cash is removed in the equity bridge; the 36c final dividend (~A$57m, not yet ex) is left in cash because a buyer today receives it.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF = reported FCF 206.834 - SBC 1.902 - interest income 13.695 - lease principal 76.215 (treatment B; lease interest 9.419 is already inside OCF). Breville dividends (A$13.9m) sit in INVESTING cash flow, so no further strip is needed for them. FY2026 owner FCF is flattered by a low cash-tax year (paid A$31.9m vs A$55.9m expense) and a capex trough (A$14.6m vs A$31.1m FY25); the component build normalises both, so year-1 modelled FCF (~A$94m) is deliberately below this A$115m print.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR statement of changes in equity / note 6 'Share-based payments expense' A$1,902k (FY25 A$4,900k). No net-share-settlement taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes KPI = 0).
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 25 July 2026 (52/53-week year ending last Saturday of July)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-24T06:10:03Z (ASX closing auction on FY2026 results day; stock +6% on the print -- results-day volatility, refresh at the next regular close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built rate: AU 10y government ~4.3% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.05 for a net-cash Australian discretionary specialty retailer = ~10.1% cost of equity; with net cash and A$69m of bank debt WACC ~= cost of equity, rounded to 10.0%. Applied identically to all three scenarios -- Smiggle turnaround risk, Australian consumer cyclicality and the two-brand concentration are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- leases as operating cost. Full lease cash cost (FY26 principal A$76.2m + lease interest A$9.4m = A$85.6m, 10.8% of revenue) charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; D&A for cash-tax EBIT is PP&E depreciation only (A$11.4m, 1.4% of revenue), NOT the A$64.8m right-of-use depreciation. The A$29.0m of variable/short-term lease rentals is already inside EBITDA as opex.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- no non-controlling interests. The 25.2% Breville associate is the reverse case: its A$34.8m equity-accounted profit (non-cash) and A$13.9m dividend are stripped from the flows and the stake is carried in the equity bridge at market value less friction (matching-asset rule, IGO.AX look-through precedent).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 2: non-US consumer operating company) on the continuing Premier Retail business (Peter Alexander + Smiggle), plus a sum-of-parts bridge for the Investment segment (Breville stake, net cash, less the already-paid interim dividend). This is a FRESH build: no prior DCF or Drivers file, no memory entry. STRUCTURAL BREAK: Just Group (Just Jeans, Jay Jays, Portmans, Dotti, Jacqui E) was sold to Myer on 26-Jan-2025 for Myer shares that were distributed in specie to Premier holders in Feb-2025 (Myer stake now nil), so every whole-company series before FY2025 describes a business Premier no longer owns; FY2026 continuing revenue A$793.7m is ~half of FY2024's A$1,595m and NPAT A$129.2m vs A$257.9m. FY0 EBITDA ANCHOR: statutory continuing EBITDA A$283.6m less associate profit 34.8 and interest revenue 14.3, plus back the 2.3 non-operating loss on Breville's share issue = A$236.8m; adding back the closed Peter Alexander UK operating loss (8.0), one-off separation costs (1.2) and half of the Peter's Dreamers launch/AASB15 deferral (4.5 of 9.1) gives an underlying pre-lease EBITDA of ~A$255m = 32.1% of revenue. The cross-check via management's pre-AASB16 EBIT ex-one-offs (A$175.9m, consolidated ~A$178.6m after eliminating the intra-group DC rent and adding property depreciation) plus PP&E depreciation and the ~A$73m rent-equivalent gives ~A$263m, so 32% is the lower end of the bracket. Year-1 base margin is set BELOW that (30.5%) because the A$36.5m TSA fee income (cost-plus-10%) is winding down with stranded-cost risk, and Smiggle's FY2027 relaunch carries marketing spend. OWNED PROPERTY (Melbourne DC and HQ) is an operating asset the retail flows already benefit from (no third-party rent), so it is NOT added to the bridge -- adding it would double count. TSA income is stripped with no matching asset because it is a fee stream that ends. Buyback: A$4.6m of the A$100m program spent by 25-Jul-2026 -- flat count is a modelling convention the company has only begun to fund. Franking credits on Premier's fully franked dividends are real value to Australian holders but are ignored per house convention.

equity_bridge.item: 25.2% Breville Group (BRG.AX) stake at market less 15% friction
equity_bridge.note: 36.50m BRG shares implied by the FY26 AR fair value A$1,081.8m at the 24-Jul-2026 close of A$29.64 (ties to 25.2% of BRG's ~144.8m shares); x A$30.56 (Yahoo BRG.AX regular close 2026-09-24) = A$1,115.4m market value; less 15% for holdco friction -- full CGT leakage on the ~A$730m embedded gain over the A$384.2m carrying value would be ~20%, an in-specie demerger (the Myer template) ~0%, and listed-stake holdco discounts typically run 10-20%. Matching-asset rule: the A$34.8m associate profit and A$13.9m dividend are OUT of the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Interim dividend A$71.8m (45c) paid 2026-08-20 out of balance-date cash
equity_bridge.note: Stock went ex on this dividend before the valuation date; the cash is in the 25-Jul-2026 balance sheet but no longer accrues to a buyer today. The 36c final (~A$57m) is not yet ex and stays in cash.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment -- terminal-rate anchor: Peter Alexander +3-4% (FY26 +3.2%, loyalty program, AU/NZ store openings) blended with a Smiggle reset (FY26 -12.9%) that base assumes only stabilises; every historical CAGR is dominated by the FY2025 Just Group divestment and the in-specie Myer distribution and describes a business Premier no longer owns.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: ALL whole-company CAGRs are structurally negative because of the Jan-2025 sale of the Apparel Brands (about half of revenue) and the Feb-2025 distribution of the Myer shares (equity fell A$1.80bn -> A$0.96bn). FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC, interest income and lease principal): FY2021 240.1, FY2023 160.0, FY2026 115.0. Continuing-operations series exists only from FY2024 (NetIncomeContinuing 185.9 -> 144.0 -> 129.2; RevenueContinuing 816.8 -> 793.7). None of these is a forward growth input; the driver paths are built bottom-up by brand.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR (-10.4% 3y) is LESS negative than reported-FCF CAGR (-15.5% 3y) only because the lease-principal deduction shrank with the divested store base; SBC is immaterial (<0.6% of revenue in every year).

base.growth_rationale: FY27: Peter Alexander +3.5% (A$565m -> ~A$585m) and Smiggle -2% (relaunch lands in 1H27 against a still-declining base) = +2.0%; FY28-29 Smiggle stabilises at +3% with PA +3.5% = +3.5%; then fades to 2.5% terminal (AU inflation-plus-population, no net store growth assumed for Smiggle).
base.margin_rationale: Pre-lease post-AASB16 EBITDA: FY26 underlying ~32.1% (see inputs.notes); FY27 30.5% absorbs TSA-fee wind-down stranded costs, Smiggle relaunch marketing and the Dreamers rewards deferral; recovers to 31.0% and holds -- no margin expansion assumed beyond re-basing after the UK exit.
base.lease_rationale: FY26 lease cash 10.8% of revenue (principal 76.2 + interest 9.4 on 793.7); drifts to 10.5% as the three PA UK stores exit (closed Aug-2026) and Smiggle's channel simplification trims the UK/Europe estate.
base.capex_da_rationale: PP&E depreciation 11.4/793.7 = 1.4% -> 1.5%; capex normalised to 2.2% (~A$18m) vs FY26 trough 1.8% and FY25 3.8%: retail segment capex 14.7 (FY26) / 19.5 (FY25), with PA AU/NZ store openings and relocations continuing.
base.tax_wc_rationale: 30% Australian statutory on positive EBIT (FY26 cash tax of A$31.9m vs A$55.9m expense is timing, not a structural shelter). Working capital: inventory-carrying retailer, net WC ~8% of revenue, so growth consumes cash (capture -8% of the revenue change).
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 14x owner FCF for a mature two-brand discretionary retailer; Gordon at 10%/2.5% (13.7x) sits just under the cap, so the two roughly agree and terminal_growth is not doing hidden work.

bull.rationale: Smiggle relaunch works: sales +8-10% in FY28-29 off the reset base while Peter Alexander compounds ~5% on the loyalty program and AU/NZ rollout; occupancy leverage takes lease cost to 10% of revenue and pre-lease EBITDA margin back to 33% (still below the ~34% the whole group ran in FY2022-24). Capex 2.5% funds the extra stores. Same WACC and cap as base.

bear.rationale: Smiggle relaunch fails to arrest the decline (another -10%/-8%/-5% before flattening) while Peter Alexander slows to +1-2% as Australian discretionary spend softens; TSA stranded costs and negative operating leverage take pre-lease EBITDA margin to 27.5% and lease cost to 11.5% of sales. Terminal growth 2.0% and a 12x cap for a shrinking-then-flat retailer. Same 10% WACC -- the risk is in these flows and in the 30% weight, not in the rate.

scenario_narratives.base: Premier is now a two-brand specialty retailer plus an investment book. The base case has Peter Alexander doing what it did in FY2026 -- record sales (+3.2%), a loyalty program that added 1.4m members in ten months, steady AU/NZ store openings -- at +3.5%/yr, and Smiggle (-12.9% in FY2026) merely stabilising after the 1H27 relaunch rather than recovering. Underlying pre-lease EBITDA margin re-bases from ~32% to 30.5% as the A$36.5m Myer transitional-services fee income winds down and relaunch spend lands, then holds at 31%. Lease cash cost stays ~10.5-10.8% of sales. Owner FCF of ~A$94m in FY27 (vs the A$115m FY26 print flattered by a low cash-tax year and a capex trough) grows to ~A$125m by FY36. The Breville stake is valued at market less 15%, net cash of A$322m less the A$72m interim dividend already paid is added. The investment book is worth roughly A$7.5/share on its own, so the market at A$11.95 is paying ~A$4.5/share -- about 5x owner FCF -- for the retail business.
scenario_narratives.bull: Smiggle's reset -- new MD, product re-aligned to the 6-12 core, channel simplification -- lands and the brand grows 8-10% off its shrunken base in FY28-29 while Peter Alexander compounds at ~5% on Peter's Dreamers and continued AU/NZ rollout. Occupancy leverage pulls lease cost to 10% of sales and pre-lease EBITDA margin recovers to 33%, still short of the group's FY2022-24 peak. Owner FCF reaches ~A$175m by FY36. Nothing in this case relies on a Breville re-rating or on corporate activity around Myer; those are unmodelled upside.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Smiggle relaunch is a multi-year fade rather than a turn -- Amazon/Temu/Kmart keep the category's value end, and sales fall a further ~20% over three years before flattening -- while Peter Alexander slows to +1-2% as higher-for-longer rates squeeze Australian discretionary spend (77% of retail revenue). Stranded shared-service costs after the Myer TSA ends and negative operating leverage compress pre-lease EBITDA margin to 27.5% with lease cost rising to 11.5% of sales. Owner FCF settles around A$70m. Even here the investment book (Breville stake, net cash) provides most of the per-share value, which is why the bear intrinsic value sits close to the current price: the market is already pricing something near this case for the retail business. Not modelled: a Breville de-rating (BRG at ~30x earnings) would cut the bridge ~A$0.9/share for every 15% fall in BRG.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted to 30% (from the 15% house default) because the central axis -- Smiggle's FY2027 relaunch -- is an unproven pivot after a 12.9% sales decline, Peter Alexander's UK expansion just failed outright (stores closed Aug-2026, A$7.7m impairment), and continuing NPAT fell 10.3% with no FY2027 guidance offered (directors invoked s299(3)). Bull cut to 20% because it needs two independent things to go right (Smiggle recovery AND PA sustaining +5%). Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position is degenerate and should be read as n/a: SBC is 0.4% of revenue, so house and street values differ by only ~A$0.25/share and the ratio explodes. Premier is effectively an SBC-zero filer; the house/street band collapses to a point.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sum-of-parts inside an owner-FCF DCF: the continuing Premier Retail flows (Peter Alexander + Smiggle) are valued on a strict owner basis -- SBC expensed, full lease cash cost inside the flows (treatment B), interest income and the Breville associate profit stripped -- and the Investment segment is added in the bridge: the 25.2% Breville stake at market less 15% friction, net cash at the 25-Jul-2026 balance date less the interim dividend already paid. Terminal value is min(Gordon, 14x owner FCF) at a 10% AUD cost of equity. Bear is weighted 30% because the Smiggle relaunch is unproven. The investment book alone is worth ~A$7.5/share, so the finding is that the market at A$11.95 is capitalising the retail business at roughly 5x owner FCF, which is a bear-case price unless one also assumes a large holdco discount on Breville.
key_risks_to_valuation: Smiggle relaunch fails (bear case): FY26 sales -12.9%, brand drifted from its 6-12 core; a further multi-year decline is the bear path and carries 30% weight

Breville mark-to-market: the stake is ~A$6/share of the bridge at BRG A$30.56 (~30x earnings); each 15% move in BRG is ~A$0.9/share, and a sale would trigger ~A$220m of CGT unless structured as an in-specie demerger
TSA stranded costs: A$36.5m of Myer transitional-services income (cost-plus-10%) is ending; shared services sized for the whole group may not shrink as fast as the fee
Australian consumer cyclicality: 77% of retail revenue is Australian discretionary spend; a downturn hits both brands and the lease cost is a fixed charge (~10.8% of sales)
Peter Alexander international execution: the UK exit (Aug-2026, A$7.7m impairment) shows the brand's offshore growth option is narrower than assumed; base assumes AU/NZ-only growth
Governance/related party: Solomon Lew controls ~42% of Premier and now sits on Myer's board with ~27% of Myer; capital allocation (Breville, Myer, buyback) is decided by a controlling shareholder
Results-day price: the A$11.95 print is the FY2026 results-day close (+6% on the day) and should be refreshed at the next regular close
